questions.question_english: According to the core tenets of behaviorism, learning is fundamentally defined as:
options_english: The active construction of internal mental schemas
The lasting change in observable behavior brought about by experience
The realization of an individual’s full potential and self-actualization
The social mediation and internalization of cultural tools
questions.explanation_english: In classical behaviorist psychology, learning is canonically defined as a relatively permanent or lasting change in observable behavior occurring as a result of experience or practice with environmental stimuli. The crucial criteria in behaviorism are that: (a) the change must manifest in observable physical actions rather than unobservable internal states, (b) it is produced by environmental interactions/conditioning (excluding biological maturation or temporary physiological states like fatigue), and (c) it demonstrates persistence over time. Active mental schema construction corresponds to cognitivism/constructivism, self-actualization to humanism, and sociocultural mediation to Vygotskian theory.
questions.explanation_hindi: व्यवहारवाद में अधिगम की मानक परिभाषा 'अनुभव या अभ्यास के परिणामस्वरूप बाह्य एवं अवलोकनीय व्यवहार में होने वाला अपेक्षाकृत स्थायी परिवर्तन' है। व्यवहारवादियों के अनुसार, अधिगम तभी माना जाता है जब वह दृश्य व्यवहार में परिलक्षित हो और जिसका वस्तुनिष्ठ मापन किया जा सके। यह परिवर्तन पर्यावरण के साथ अंतःक्रिया अथवा अनुकूलन से उत्पन्न होना चाहिए (न कि केवल शारीरिक परिपक्वता, थकान या मादक पदार्थों से)। आंतरिक स्कीमा का निर्माण संज्ञानवाद का विषय है, आत्म-साक्षात्कार मानवतावाद से संबंधित है, और सामाजिक मध्यस्थता वायगोत्स्की के सिद्धांत से जुड़ी है। अतः विकल्प (B) सही है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) The lasting change in behavior through experience

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Behaviorist theory defines learning fundamentally as a persistent transformation in observable performance resulting from interaction with environmental conditions. This paradigm focuses on measurable stimulus-response associations formed through systematic conditioning procedures, maintaining that behavioral change must be demonstrably observable while dismissing internal mental constructs, unobservable cognitive processes, or subjective self-reports of learning.

I. गृहकार्य पूरा न करने पर कक्षा के सामने छात्र को डांटना।

III. एक छात्र से 50 बार माफीनामा पत्र लिखवाना।
IV. व्याख्यान के दौरान उपयोग किए गए छात्र के मोबाइल फोन को जब्त करना।

questions.question_english:
Consider the following disciplinary actions taken in a school:
I. Scolding a student in front of the class for not completing homework.
II. Taking away a student’s sports period for bullying a peer.
III. Making a student write an apology letter 50 times.
IV. Confiscating a student’s mobile phone used during a lecture.
Which of the above are examples of Negative Punishment?
options_english: I and III only
II and IV only
I, II, and IV only
III and IV only
questions.explanation_english:
Negative punishment involves removing a pleasant stimulus or privilege to decrease an unwanted behavior:
- II (Taking away sports period) revokes a valued privilege -> Negative Punishment.
- IV (Confiscating mobile phone) removes a valued personal possession -> Negative Punishment.
In contrast:
- I (Scolding publicly) introduces an aversive verbal stimulus -> Positive Punishment.
- III (Writing apology letter 50 times) adds an unpleasant penalty task -> Positive Punishment.
Therefore, only actions II and IV represent negative punishment.
questions.explanation_hindi:
नकारात्मक दंड में अवांछित व्यवहार को कम करने के लिए किसी सुखद विशेषाधिकार या उद्दीपक को वापस ले लिया जाता है:
- II. खेल के कालांश को छीनना: छात्र को एक पसंदीदा गतिविधि से वंचित किया गया -> नकारात्मक दंड।
- IV. मोबाइल फोन जब्त करना: छात्र से उसकी पसंदीदा वस्तु ले ली गई -> नकारात्मक दंड।
इसके विपरीत:
- I. कक्षा के सामने डांटना: एक अप्रिय मौखिक उद्दीपक प्रस्तुत किया गया -> सकारात्मक दंड।
- III. 50 बार माफीनामा लिखवाना: एक अतिरिक्त अप्रिय कार्य थोपा गया -> सकारात्मक दंड।
अतः केवल II और IV नकारात्मक दंड के उदाहरण हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) II and IV only

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Negative punishment requires withdrawing desirable stimuli or privileges following unwanted conduct. Confiscating a personal device and revoking sports participation remove pleasant privileges, illustrating negative punishment. Conversely, scolding or assigning extra writing adds unpleasant stimuli, representing positive punishment designed to suppress disruptive actions through direct presentation of aversive consequences.

questions.question_english: In Piaget's theory of cognitive development, which of the following best describes what occurs to mental schemas during the internal process of 'organization'?
options_english: They are permanently erased and purged from memory when cognitive disequilibrium arises
They are converted exclusively into overt motor reflexes through repetitive behavioral drills
They become rigid, isolated mental templates that resist any future developmental modification
They are internally rearranged, interconnected, and integrated with other schemas into a cohesive cognitive system
questions.explanation_english: Piaget identified two primary, invariant cognitive functions that drive intellectual growth: 'adaptation' (consisting of assimilation and accommodation, which mediate direct interactions with the external environment) and 'organization' (an internal, reflective process). Unlike adaptation, organization occurs entirely within the mind. During organization, the learner internally rearranges, classifies, and synthesizes separate schemas, integrating them into higher-order, coordinated, and interconnected cognitive networks. For example, an infant initially has distinct, isolated schemas for looking at an object and grasping an object; through organization, these two separate sensorimotor schemas are combined into a higher-order 'visually guided reaching' schema. In older learners, conceptual schemas (such as velocity, mass, and acceleration) are organized into an integrated mental model of Newtonian mechanics.
questions.explanation_hindi: जीन पियाजे के अनुसार संज्ञानात्मक विकास के दो मूलभूत अपरिवर्तनीय कार्य (Invariant Functions) होते हैं: 'अनुकूलन' (Adaptation - जो आत्मसातीकरण और समायोजन के माध्यम से पर्यावरण के साथ सीधा संपर्क स्थापित करता है) तथा 'संगठन' (Organization - जो एक पूर्णतः आंतरिक संज्ञानात्मक प्रक्रिया है)। 'संगठन' की प्रक्रिया में व्यक्ति अपने विभिन्न पृथक स्कीमाओं को आंतरिक रूप से पुनर्व्यवस्थित करता है, उनका वर्गीकरण करता है और उन्हें एक सुसंबद्ध, परस्पर जुड़ी हुई और उच्च-स्तरीय बौद्धिक संरचना में एकीकृत करता है। उदाहरण के लिए, शैशवावस्था में बालक के पास देखने का अलग स्कीमा और पकड़ने का अलग स्कीमा होता है; संगठन के माध्यम से वह इन दोनों को जोड़कर 'दृष्टि-निर्देशित पकड़' (visually guided reaching) का एक समन्वित स्कीमा बना लेता है। इसी प्रकार उच्च कक्षाओं में भौतिकी के विभिन्न नियम संगठित होकर एक समग्र वैज्ञानिक दृष्टिकोण का निर्माण करते हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) They are internally rearranged and linked with other schemas into an interconnected system.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Organization is an internal cognitive process wherein schemas are systematically rearranged, differentiated, and connected into a coherent mental framework. This structural integration allows for efficient access, retrieval, and application of knowledge across domains.

questions.question_hindi:
शैक्षिक मनोविज्ञान में संज्ञानवाद (Cognitivism) के सैद्धांतिक सिद्धांतों के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
I. अधिगम को सूचनाओं को सक्रिय रूप से ग्रहण करने, व्यवस्थित करने और संसाधित करने की एक आंतरिक प्रक्रिया माना जाता है।
II. ज्ञान मस्तिष्क में 'स्कीमा' (schemas) नामक परस्पर संबद्ध संज्ञानात्मक संजालों में संरचित होता है।
III. पर्यावरणीय उद्दीपक बिना किसी आंतरिक मानसिक मध्यस्थता के अधिगम को प्रत्यक्ष और निश्चित रूप से नियंत्रित करते हैं।
IV. बहु-स्तरीय स्मृति प्रणालियाँ (memory systems) अधिगम की प्रक्रिया में एक केंद्रीय संरचनात्मक भूमिका निभाती हैं।
उपर्युक्त कथनों में से कौन-से सही हैं?
options_hindi: केवल I, II और III
केवल I, II और IV
केवल II, III और IV
केवल I, III और IV

questions.question_english:
Consider the following theoretical propositions concerning Cognitivism in educational psychology:
I. Learning is conceptualized as an active internal process of receiving, organizing, and transforming information.
II. Knowledge is structured within interconnected cognitive networks termed 'schemas'.
III. Environmental stimuli directly and deterministically control learning in the total absence of internal mental mediation.
IV. Multi-store memory systems play a central architectural role in the learning process.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options_english: I, II, and III only
I, II, and IV only
II, III, and IV only
I, III, and IV only
questions.explanation_english: Statements I, II, and IV are defining tenets of Cognitivism: (I) Cognitivism views the learner as an active information processor who attends to, encodes, and interprets environmental data; (II) Acquired knowledge is organized into cognitive architectures known as schemas (mental frameworks or knowledge networks); (IV) Human memory systems—sensory register, limited-capacity working memory, and permanent long-term memory—are central to explaining how learning occurs, is retained, and is retrieved. Statement III is completely antithetical to cognitivism; it describes the radical environmental determinism of Radical Behaviorism (the direct S-R model). Cognitivism replaced direct stimulus control with the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) paradigm, demonstrating that internal mental processes mediate all responses. Therefore, only I, II, and IV are correct.
questions.explanation_hindi: कथन I, II और IV संज्ञानवाद (Cognitivism) के मूलभूत स्तंभ हैं: (I) संज्ञानवाद शिक्षार्थी को एक सक्रिय सूचना प्रसंसाधक (active processor) मानता है जो ज्ञान का सक्रिय रूप से संकलन और संगठन करता है; (II) ज्ञान मस्तिष्क में 'स्कीमा' (schemas) यानी मानसिक संरचनाओं के रूप में व्यवस्थित होता है; (IV) संवेदी स्मृति, कार्यशील स्मृति और दीर्घकालिक स्मृति जैसी प्रणालियाँ अधिगम की प्रक्रिया में केंद्रीय भूमिका निभाती हैं। इसके विपरीत, कथन III कट्टर व्यवहारवाद (Radical Behaviorism) की मान्यता है, जो यह दावा करता है कि उद्दीपक बिना किसी मानसिक मध्यस्थता के सीधे व्यवहार को नियंत्रित करते हैं। संज्ञानवाद ने इस यांत्रिक S-R दृष्टिकोण को खारिज करते हुए सिद्ध किया कि उद्दीपक और अनुक्रिया के बीच आंतरिक मानसिक प्रक्रियाएँ मध्यस्थता करती हैं। अतः केवल I, II और IV सही हैं।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) I, II, and IV only

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Cognitivism posits that learning involves active mental processing, organizing knowledge into cognitive schemas, and utilizing memory systems effectively. Cognitivist theory rejects the behaviorist premise that environmental stimuli directly control behavior without cognitive mediation, emphasizing instead that internal mental structures mediate learning outcomes and understanding.

questions.question_english: While designing a modern science curriculum, a Principal draws upon Jerome Bruner's cognitive pedagogy to emphasize that effective instruction must empower learners to infer, deduce, and generalize beyond direct instruction. Bruner famously termed this cognitive process as:
options_english: Operant shaping of terminal behaviors
Going beyond the information given
Thorndike's law of affective readiness
Piagetian equilibration of cognitive structures
questions.explanation_english: One of Jerome Bruner's most seminal contributions to cognitive psychology and pedagogy is the concept of 'going beyond the information given' (which was also the title of his acclaimed 1973 book). Bruner argued that true intellectual competence does not consist of merely cataloging and reciting presented facts; rather, it involves acquiring structural principles and coding systems that empower the learner to make inferences, extrapolate trends, predict unobserved events, and solve novel problems. In science education, when students understand underlying core concepts (such as density, thermodynamics, or genetics), they can readily predict how a system will behave in unfamiliar scenarios—thereby 'going beyond the information given.'
questions.explanation_hindi: जेरोम ब्रूनर के संज्ञानात्मक मनोविज्ञान और शिक्षाशास्त्र में सबसे प्रसिद्ध विचारों में से एक 'दी गई सूचना से आगे जाना' (Going beyond the information given) की संकल्पना है (जो उनकी 1973 की प्रसिद्ध पुस्तक का शीर्षक भी थी)। ब्रूनर के अनुसार, वास्तविक अधिगम का अर्थ केवल शिक्षक द्वारा बताए गए तथ्यों को याद करना या दोहराना नहीं है, बल्कि विषय की अंतर्निहित संरचना और सामान्य सिद्धांतों को इस प्रकार समझना है कि छात्र स्वयं नए निष्कर्ष निकाल सकें, भविष्यवाणियाँ कर सकें और अज्ञात समस्याओं का समाधान ढूँढ सकें। विज्ञान शिक्षण में जब विद्यार्थी मूल सिद्धांतों (जैसे घनत्व या ऊर्जा संरक्षण) को समझ लेते हैं, तो वे नई परिस्थितियों में उसके प्रभाव का स्वयं अनुमान लगा लेते हैं—यही 'दी गई सूचना से आगे जाने' की क्षमता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (B) Going beyond the information given

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Bruner described effective instruction as enabling learners to go beyond the information given. This capacity involves drawing inferences, predicting outcomes, and extrapolating generalized rules from specific structured learning experiences.

questions.question_hindi:
विद्यालयी परिवेश में शास्त्रीय अनुकूलन (क्लासिकल कंडीशनिंग) के संबंध में निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:

options_hindi: केवल I
केवल II

questions.question_english: Which statement best distinguishes assimilation from accommodation in Piaget's cognitive theory?

questions.explanation_english:
In Jean Piaget's theory of cognitive development, adaptation occurs through the complementary interplay of assimilation and accommodation:
- Assimilation is a quantitative expansion process wherein an individual incorporates, interprets, and fits new incoming environmental information into pre-existing mental schemas without fundamentally changing the underlying structure of those schemas. The mind bends reality to fit its current knowledge.
- Accommodation is a qualitative reorganization process wherein existing cognitive schemas prove inadequate to explain novel experiences, compelling the individual to adjust, expand, or build entirely new schemas to fit the reality of the external world.
Together, balanced by equilibration, assimilation and accommodation allow learners to build increasingly sophisticated and coherent understandings of their world. Options A, B, and C present fundamentally distorted representations of cognitive developmental theory.

Assimilation integrates incoming environmental information directly into established mental structures, whereas accommodation modifies or creates schemas when new data conflicts with existing cognitive frameworks.

questions.question_english: The core epistemological premise of Constructivism is that:
options_english: Knowledge exists entirely independently of the human learner and must be directly transmitted by teachers.
Knowledge is innately pre-programmed into human biological genetics and unfolds automatically over time.
Knowledge is actively constructed through experience.
Knowledge is acquired solely through external environmental reinforcement schedules and conditioning.
questions.explanation_english: Epistemology addresses the philosophical questions of what knowledge is and how it is acquired. The central epistemological thesis of Constructivism (advanced by theorists such as Jean Piaget, Lev Vygotsky, and Jerome Bruner) is that knowledge is not a passive mirror of an external reality that can be directly transmitted or poured into a learner's mind. Nor is it purely hard-wired biologically. Rather, knowledge is actively constructed and dynamically restructured by the learner as they interact with, interpret, and make sense of their physical, cognitive, and social experiences. Option A reflects objectivist/traditional transmission pedagogy; Option B describes extreme nativism/biological determinism; and Option D represents behaviorism. Hence, Option C is correct.

questions.question_english:
Consider the following sub-stages of Jean Piaget's Sensorimotor stage:
I. Simple Reflexes
II. Primary Circular Reactions
III. Secondary Circular Reactions
IV. Coordination of Secondary Schemas
Which of the following represents the correct developmental sequence of these sub-stages?
options_english: I, II, III, IV
II, I, III, IV
I, III, II, IV
IV, III, II, I
questions.explanation_english:
Jean Piaget subdivided the Sensorimotor Stage (birth to 24 months) into six sequential sub-stages:
1. Sub-stage 1 (Birth to 1 month): Simple Reflexes (e.g., sucking, rooting, grasping reflexes).
2. Sub-stage 2 (1 to 4 months): First habits and Primary Circular Reactions (repetitive actions centered around the infant's own body that initially occurred by chance, such as thumb-sucking).
3. Sub-stage 3 (4 to 8 months): Secondary Circular Reactions (infants repeat actions centered on the external environment to produce interesting results, such as shaking a rattle).
4. Sub-stage 4 (8 to 12 months): Coordination of Secondary Schemas (intentionality, combining schemas into goal-directed behaviour, and early object permanence).
5. Sub-stage 5 (12 to 18 months): Tertiary Circular Reactions (curiosity and active trial-and-error experimentation with objects).
6. Sub-stage 6 (18 to 24 months): Internalization of Schemas / Mental Representations (symbolic thought and insight).
Therefore, the correct chronological sequence of the given four sub-stages is I -> II -> III -> IV. Hence, Option A is correct.
questions.explanation_hindi:
जीन पियाजे ने संवेदी-गामक अवस्था (जन्म से 2 वर्ष) को छह क्रमिक उप-चरणों में विभाजित किया है:
1. उप-चरण 1 (जन्म से 1 माह): सरल प्रतिवर्त क्रियाएँ (Simple Reflexes)—जैसे चूसना, पकड़ना और निगलना।
2. उप-चरण 2 (1 से 4 माह): प्राथमिक वृत्तीय प्रतिक्रियाएँ (Primary Circular Reactions)—शिशु के अपने शरीर पर केंद्रित सुखद क्रियाओं की पुनरावृत्ति (जैसे अंगूठा चूसना)।
3. उप-चरण 3 (4 से 8 माह): द्वितीयक वृत्तीय प्रतिक्रियाएँ (Secondary Circular Reactions)—बाह्य वातावरण की वस्तुओं पर केंद्रित क्रियाओं की पुनरावृत्ति (जैसे खिलौने या झुनझुने को बार-बार हिलाना)।
4. उप-चरण 4 (8 से 12 माह): द्वितीयक योजनाओं का समन्वय (Coordination of Secondary Schemas)—उद्देश्यपूर्ण या लक्ष्य-निर्देशित व्यवहार तथा दो क्रियाओं का संयोजन।
5. उप-चरण 5 (12 से 18 माह): तृतीयक वृत्तीय प्रतिक्रियाएँ (Tertiary Circular Reactions)—नवीन साधनों की खोज और सक्रिय प्रयोग (Trial and error)।
6. उप-चरण 6 (18 से 24 माह): मानसिक संयोजन और आंतरिक प्रतिमान (Mental Representations)।
अतः दिए गए चार उप-चरणों का सही क्रम I -> II -> III -> IV है। विकल्प A सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) I, II, III, IV

questions.question_english: The foundational paradigm shift from Behaviorism to Cognitivism in educational psychology during the mid-twentieth century fundamentally involved a redirection of focus from:
options_english: Internal cognitive architecture to externally observable behavioral responses
Social collaborative learning to individualized mechanical drill worksheets
Extrinsic motivational drives to basic physiological survival needs
Observable external behavior to covert internal mental processes
questions.explanation_english: The 'Cognitive Revolution' of the late 1950s and 1960s represented a monumental epistemological shift in psychology. Behaviorism had dogmatically restricted the focus of psychology to externally observable, measurable behaviors and environmental contingencies, explicitly rejecting internal mental operations as unscientific 'black box' phenomena. Cognitivism overturned this restriction, redirecting scientific attention toward the unobservable, covert internal mental processes that mediate human learning—including perception, selective attention, information encoding, memory storage, retrieval mechanisms, schema construction, and metacognitive problem solving. Thus, the transition was a historic move from overt observable behavior to covert internal mental operations.
questions.explanation_hindi: 1950 और 1960 के दशक की 'संज्ञानात्मक क्रांति' (Cognitive Revolution) शैक्षिक मनोविज्ञान में एक युगांतकारी परिवर्तन लेकर आई। इससे पूर्व व्यवहारवाद का बोलबाला था, जो केवल बाह्य रूप से दिखाई देने वाले प्रेक्षणीय व्यवहार (observable behavior) तथा उद्दीपक-अनुक्रिया संबंधों को ही विज्ञान मानता था और मस्तिष्क को 'ब्लैक बॉक्स' कहता था। संज्ञानवाद ने इस संकीर्ण दृष्टिकोण को बदलते हुए मनोविज्ञान का केंद्र बिंदु बाह्य प्रेक्षणीय व्यवहार से हटाकर 'आंतरिक मानसिक प्रक्रियाओं' (internal mental processes)—जैसे अवधान, प्रत्यक्षीकरण, सूचना प्रक्रमण, स्मृति संचयन, स्कीमा निर्माण और समस्या-समाधान की ओर स्थानांतरित किया। अतः विकल्प D सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) Observable behavior to internal mental processes.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: The cognitive revolution marked a paradigm shift in educational psychology from behaviorism to cognitivism. This movement redirected theoretical focus from measuring external observable behaviors and environmental reinforcement schedules toward investigating internal mental operations, including attention, information encoding, memory storage, retrieval mechanisms, and problem-solving strategies.

questions.question_english: A student who consistently speaks out of turn in class is ignored by the teacher. Eventually, the student stops interrupting. The teacher’s strategy is an application of:
options_english: Negative reinforcement
Positive punishment
Extinction
Negative punishment
questions.explanation_english: The teacher's planned ignoring is a classic application of operant extinction. In classroom settings, attention-seeking disruptive behaviors are typically maintained and reinforced by teacher reactions or peer attention. When the reinforcing consequence (attention) is systematically withheld, the conditioned behavior gradually declines in frequency and is eventually extinguished altogether.
questions.explanation_hindi: शिक्षक द्वारा योजनाबद्ध तरीके से ध्यान न देना (Planned Ignoring) क्रियाप्रसूत अनुबंधन में विलोपन (Extinction) का प्रत्यक्ष अनुप्रयोग है। कक्षा में ध्यान आकर्षित करने वाले व्यवधान प्रायः शिक्षक या सहपाठियों के ध्यान द्वारा ही पुनर्बलित होते हैं। जब उस व्यवहार को बनाए रखने वाले पुनर्बलन (ध्यान/प्रतिक्रिया) को पूरी तरह रोक दिया जाता है, तो व्यवहार की आवृत्ति में क्रमिक रूप से गिरावट आती है और वह व्यवहार अंततः समाप्त हो जाता है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Extinction

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Withholding attention or reinforcement for attention-seeking behaviors directly applies operant extinction. When unwanted interruptions that were previously reinforced by peer or teacher attention are systematically met with planned ignoring, the behavior loses its maintaining consequences, causing the frequency of vocal disruptions to gradually decline and eventually cease altogether within the classroom.

questions.question_english: In the psychology of learning, Edward Thorndike's concept of learning by 'Trial and Error' fundamentally implies that learning occurs through:
options_english: Sudden mental insight into the overarching structural relationships of a complex problem situation
Systematic observation and active imitation of a skilled expert model within the social environment
The gradual stamping in of correct responses and the systematic stamping out of incorrect ones
Active and dynamic restructuring of internal cognitive schemas and mental representations
questions.explanation_english: Thorndike's Trial-and-Error theory posits that learning is an incremental, mechanical process rather than an instantaneous cognitive revelation. When confronted with an unfamiliar challenge, an organism executes diverse exploratory behaviors. Unsuccessful actions that fail to alleviate the dilemma produce annoyance or neutral consequences and are progressively eliminated—a phenomenon Thorndike designated as 'stamping out'. Conversely, actions that accidentally resolve the situation yield satisfaction and are progressively reinforced—designated as 'stamping in'. Over successive iterations, errors decrease in a continuous mathematical progression until the optimal stimulus-response connection is firmly established. This incremental model contrasts directly with Gestalt insight learning (Köhler), social modeling (Bandura), and constructivist schema equilibration (Piaget).
questions.explanation_hindi: थार्नडाइक का 'प्रयास एवं त्रुटि' (Trial and Error) सिद्धांत यह स्पष्ट करता है कि अधिगम अचानक अंतर्दृष्टि या बौद्धिक छलांग से नहीं होता, बल्कि यह एक क्रमिक और यांत्रिक प्रक्रिया है। जब कोई प्राणी किसी नई समस्या का सामना करता है, तो वह कई प्रकार की यादृच्छिक व अन्वेषणात्मक क्रियाएँ करता है। जो क्रियाएँ लक्ष्य प्राप्ति में व्यर्थ सिद्ध होती हैं या असंतोष उत्पन्न करती हैं, वे धीरे-धीरे समाप्त हो जाती हैं—इसे थार्नडाइक ने 'अनुक्रियाओं का विलोपन' (stamping out) कहा। वहीं दूसरी ओर, जो क्रियाएँ समस्या का समाधान करती हैं और संतोष प्रदान करती हैं, वे मस्तिष्क में स्थायी रूप से स्थापित हो जाती हैं—इसे 'अनुक्रियाओं का अंकन/सुदृढ़ीकरण' (stamping in) कहा गया। अभ्यास के साथ त्रुटियों की संख्या घटती जाती है और अंततः उद्दीपक तथा सही अनुक्रिया के बीच सुदृढ़ संबंध बन जाता है। (विकल्प A गेस्टाल्ट अंतर्दृष्टि, B सामाजिक अधिगम तथा D पियाजे के रचनावाद से संबंधित हैं)।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Gradual stamping in of correct responses and stamping out of incorrect ones.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Thorndike’s trial-and-error learning principle posits that organisms solve novel problems through varied exploratory movements rather than sudden cognitive insight. Successful actions leading to satisfying outcomes are gradually stamped in or reinforced, whereas unsuccessful actions are stamped out, leading to progressive reductions in error rates over successive problem-solving trials.

questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the overview of major learning theories:
I. Behaviorists argue that internal mental states are irrelevant or unnecessary for understanding learning.
II. Cognitivists use the metaphor of the human mind as an information processor.
III. Humanistic theories emphasize self-actualization and the affective domain.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
options_english: I and II only
II and III only
I and III only
I, II, and III
questions.explanation_english:
All three statements (I, II, and III) are correct:
1. Statement I is correct: Radical behaviorists like Watson and Skinner argued that because internal mental states (thoughts, motives, introspection) cannot be objectively observed or measured, they should be excluded from scientific psychology, focusing purely on observable stimulus-response contingencies.
2. Statement II is correct: The cognitive paradigm conceptualizes the mind using the computer metaphor (information processing model), examining sensory input, encoding, storage in working/long-term memory, and retrieval.
3. Statement III is correct: Humanistic psychology (Carl Rogers, Abraham Maslow) prioritizes individual potential, self-actualization, subjective human experience, intrinsic motivation, and emotional/affective well-being in educational environments.
Therefore, option (D) is the correct answer.
questions.explanation_hindi:
कथन I, II और III तीनों सही हैं:
1. कथन I सही है: व्यवहारवादी (जैसे वाटसन और स्किनर) यह मानते हैं कि मन और आंतरिक मानसिक दशाओं को प्रत्यक्ष रूप से देखा या मापा नहीं जा सकता, इसलिए अधिगम की वैज्ञानिक समझ के लिए केवल अवलोकनीय उद्दीपक और अनुक्रिया ही प्रासंगिक हैं।
2. कथन II सही है: संज्ञानवाद ने कंप्यूटर के उद्भव के साथ मानव मस्तिष्क की तुलना एक सूचना संसाधक (Information Processor) से की, जो इनपुट ग्रहण करता है, कूटबद्ध (encode) करता है, स्मृति में संचित करता है और आवश्यकता पड़ने पर पुनर्प्राप्त करता है।
3. कथन III सही है: मानवतावादी सिद्धांत (अब्राहम मैस्लो, कार्ल रोजर्स) शिक्षार्थी के भावात्मक पक्ष, व्यक्तिगत स्वायत्तता, आंतरिक प्रेरणा और आत्म-साक्षात्कार (Self-actualization) पर सर्वाधिक बल देते हैं।
अतः सही उत्तर विकल्प (D) है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (D) I, II, and III

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Major paradigms in learning theory examine human development through unique conceptual lenses. Behaviorists emphasize externally observable actions while treating internal cognitive states as unobservable. Cognitivists conceptualize human cognition using an information-processing architecture akin to computer operations. Humanistic framework theorists prioritize affective development, subjective personal experience, intrinsic motivation, self-directed agency, and the pursuit of individual self-actualization.

questions.question_english: According to Skinner’s operant conditioning, positive punishment involves:
options_english: Delivering an unpleasant stimulus to reduce a behavior.
Removing a highly desirable stimulus after a behavior to decrease its overall occurrence.
Presenting a highly desirable stimulus after a behavior to increase its overall occurrence.
Removing an unwelcome aversive stimulus after a behavior to increase its overall occurrence.
questions.explanation_english: In operant conditioning, the modifier 'positive' signifies the delivery or addition of an environmental stimulus, while 'punishment' denotes the functional outcome of decreasing or suppressing a behavior. Therefore, positive punishment fundamentally involves administering an unpleasant or aversive stimulus (e.g., a formal reprimand or extra chore) immediately following an undesirable response to reduce the future probability of that response.
questions.explanation_hindi: क्रियाप्रसूत अनुबंधन में 'सकारात्मक' (Positive) शब्द का अर्थ उद्दीपक को 'जोड़ना या प्रस्तुत करना' है, जबकि 'दंड' (Punishment) का अर्थ व्यवहार को 'घटाना या दबाना' है। अतः सकारात्मक दंड से तात्पर्य किसी अवांछित व्यवहार के घटित होने पर किसी अप्रिय या कष्टप्रद उद्दीपक (जैसे डांटना, चेतावनी देना या अतिरिक्त कार्य सौंपना) को प्रस्तुत करने से है, ताकि भविष्य में वह व्यवहार पुनः न दोहराया जाए।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Delivering an unpleasant stimulus to reduce a behavior.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Positive punishment involves presenting an aversive stimulus immediately following an undesired behavior to reduce the future likelihood of that behavior occurring. The term positive indicates the addition or delivery of a consequence, while punishment indicates that the ultimate functional outcome is the suppression or decrease of the target behavior’s frequency.

questions.question_english: To mitigate the drawbacks of pure discovery learning, modern pedagogy often employs 'Guided Discovery.' This instructional method primarily involves:
options_english: Providing hints and structured questions to steer inquiry.
The teacher explicitly and directly telling the students beforehand exactly what they will discover.
Allowing students to aimlessly wander the library without any specific structured learning objective.
Completely replacing all practical laboratory work with passive textbook reading assignments.
questions.explanation_english: Guided Discovery strikes an optimal instructional balance between student-centered exploratory autonomy and teacher-led cognitive support. Recognizing that pure, unguided discovery frequently leads to cognitive overload and misconceptions, guided discovery incorporates instructional scaffolding. The educator provides carefully designed tasks, timely hints, leading questions, and procedural cues that guide learners toward fundamental principles without outright revealing the solutions. This keeps the inquiry within the students' cognitive reach while preserving the cognitive and motivational benefits of personal discovery. Option B describes direct exposition; Option C is chaotic unguided discovery; Option D is traditional passive reception. Hence, Option A is correct.
questions.explanation_hindi: निर्देशित खोज (Guided Discovery) पूर्णतः अनिर्देशित खोज की कमियों (संज्ञानात्मक अधिभार, भ्रांतियाँ और समय की बर्बादी) को दूर करने का एक प्रभावी शैक्षणिक समाधान है। इसमें शिक्षक छात्रों की स्वतंत्र जांच को पूरी तरह समाप्त नहीं करता, बल्कि उन्हें ऐसे रणनीतिक संकेत (hints), दिशा-निर्देशक प्रश्न और पाड़ (scaffolding) प्रदान करता है जो उनकी सोच को सही दिशा में आगे बढ़ाते हैं। इससे छात्र स्वयं उत्तर तक पहुँचने का अनुभव प्राप्त करते हैं, जबकि संज्ञानात्मक भार उनकी क्षमता के भीतर बना रहता है। विकल्प B प्रत्यक्ष निर्देश को दर्शाता है; विकल्प C दिशाहीन अधिगम है; और विकल्प D पारंपरिक निष्क्रिय अध्ययन है। अतः विकल्प A सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Providing hints and structured questions to steer inquiry.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Guided discovery balances student inquiry with structured scaffolding. Educators provide targeted prompts, cues, and strategic questions that steer exploration while keeping cognitive demands manageable.

questions.question_english: A major cognitive milestone achieved during the sensorimotor stage is the realization that objects and people continue to exist even when they are not physically visible, audible, or tangible. This concept is known as:
options_english: Object permanence
Conservation of mass
Perceptual centration
Adolescent egocentrism
questions.explanation_english: "Object Permanence" (often termed the object concept by Piaget) is the cognitive understanding that objects, persons, and events continue to exist in space and time independently of one's immediate perception or action upon them. In early infancy (under 4 to 8 months), out of sight is literally out of mind—if an attractive toy is covered with a blanket, the baby behaves as if it has ceased to exist and stops searching. By around 8 to 12 months, infants begin actively searching for hidden items, and by 18 to 24 months, complete object permanence is achieved. This milestone is profound because it marks the birth of mental representation and symbolic memory, laying the groundwork for language development and preoperational thought. Hence, Option A is correct.
questions.explanation_hindi: 'वस्तु स्थायित्व' (Object Permanence) का अर्थ यह समझना है कि वस्तुएँ और व्यक्ति प्रत्यक्ष संवेदी संपर्क से परे भी अपना स्वतंत्र अस्तित्व बनाए रखते हैं। प्रारंभिक शैशवावस्था (लगभग 4 से 8 माह से पूर्व) में बच्चे के लिए "दृष्टि से ओझल, तो अस्तित्व से ओझल" की स्थिति होती है; यदि किसी खिलौने को कपड़े से ढक दिया जाए तो शिशु उसे खोजना बंद कर देता है मानो वह गायब हो गया हो। लगभग 8 से 12 माह की आयु में बच्चा छिपी हुई वस्तु को खोजने का प्रयास करता है और 18 से 24 माह तक वस्तु स्थायित्व पूरी तरह विकसित हो जाता है। यह उपलब्धि इसलिए क्रांतिकारी है क्योंकि यह शिशु के मस्तिष्क में 'आंतरिक मानसिक प्रतिमान' (Mental Representation) के उदय का प्रमाण है, जो आगे चलकर भाषा और प्रतीकात्मक चिंतन का आधार बनता है। अतः विकल्प A सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (A) Object permanence

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Object permanence is a fundamental cognitive milestone achieved toward the end of the sensorimotor stage. It describes a child's understanding that physical objects and people continue to exist even when they are out of sight, unheard, or untouched, marking the emergence of internal mental representation.

questions.question_english: According to constructivist theories, 'misconceptions' or 'alternative frameworks' held by students are viewed as:
options_english: Clear and undeniable evidence of low innate intellectual ability in students.
Incorrect target behaviors that must be penalized immediately to be extinguished.
Natural stepping stones in meaning-making to be restructured.
Completely irrelevant phenomena that have no bearing on the learning process.
questions.explanation_english: In traditional and behaviorist paradigms, student misconceptions were seen as undesirable errors or signs of academic ignorance that had to be stamped out through rote drilling and negative feedback. Constructivist theory radically reframes this view. Constructivism recognizes that learners continuously construct intuitive, sensible models ('naive theories' or 'alternative frameworks') to explain their physical and social worlds (e.g., believing that heavy objects fall faster than light ones). Rather than defects, these frameworks represent natural developmental stepping stones in the cognitive process of meaning-making. Effective constructivist pedagogy values them as diagnostic windows into student thinking and creates cognitive dissonance to guide learners in restructuring their schemas toward scientific accuracy. Hence, Option C is correct.
questions.explanation_hindi: पारंपरिक और व्यवहारवादी शिक्षण प्रतिमानों में छात्रों की गलतियों या भ्रांतियों को अज्ञानता का लक्षण या अवांछित व्यवहार माना जाता था जिसे तुरंत सुधारने या दंडित करने की आवश्यकता होती थी। इसके विपरीत, रचनावादी सिद्धांत यह मानता है कि बच्चे अपने दैनिक अनुभवों के आधार पर दुनिया को समझने के लिए अपनी स्वयं की सहज और आंतरिक रूप से तार्किक रूपरेखाएं बनाते हैं, जिन्हें 'वैकल्पिक अवधारणाएं' (Alternative Frameworks) कहा जाता है। रचनावाद इन भ्रांतियों को बुद्धि की कमी नहीं, बल्कि अर्थ-निर्माण की यात्रा में स्वाभाविक सोपान (Stepping stones) मानता है। ये भ्रांतियां शिक्षक को यह समझने में मदद करती हैं कि छात्र कैसे सोच रहा है, जिससे शिक्षक संज्ञानात्मक असंतुलन (Cognitive Dissonance) पैदा करके छात्र की स्कीमा को पुनर्गठित करने में मार्गदर्शन कर सकता है। अतः विकल्प C सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) Natural stepping stones in meaning-making to be restructured.

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: Constructivism views student misconceptions as natural developmental stepping stones that reveal current cognitive models, serving as valuable opportunities for instructional intervention and schema restructuring.

questions.question_english: Which of the following educational psychologists formulated the theory of "Meaningful Reception Learning", proposing that new knowledge must be anchored to existing concepts within the learner's cognitive structure?
options_english: B.F. Skinner
Ivan Pavlov
David Ausubel
Albert Bandura
questions.explanation_english: David Ausubel (1918–2008) formulated the theory of Meaningful Verbal Learning and Meaningful Reception Learning. He famously stated: "The most important single factor influencing learning is what the learner already knows. Ascertain this and teach him accordingly." Ausubel distinguished meaningful learning from rote memorization, emphasizing that true cognitive assimilation (subsumption) occurs when new information is non-arbitrarily and substantively connected to pre-existing relevant concepts (anchoring ideas) in the learner's cognitive structure. To facilitate this anchoring process, Ausubel introduced the instructional tool known as the "Advance Organizer"—introductory material presented prior to learning that bridges the gap between what the learner already knows and what needs to be learned. In contrast, Skinner and Pavlov developed behavioural conditioning models, while Bandura formulated social cognitive theory. Hence, Option C is correct.
questions.explanation_hindi: डेविड आसुबेल (David Ausubel) ने 'सार्थक शाब्दिक अधिगम' (Meaningful Verbal Learning) और 'सार्थक ग्रहण अधिगम' का सिद्धांत प्रतिपादित किया। उनका प्रसिद्ध कथन है: "अधिगम को प्रभावित करने वाला सबसे महत्वपूर्ण एकल कारक वह है जो शिक्षार्थी पहले से जानता है। इसका पता लगाइए और तदनुसार उसे पढ़ाइए।" आसुबेल ने रटकर सीखने (Rote learning) और सार्थक अधिगम (Meaningful learning) के बीच स्पष्ट अंतर किया। उन्होंने बताया कि सार्थक अधिगम तब होता है जब नया ज्ञान शिक्षार्थी के मस्तिष्क में पहले से उपस्थित प्रासंगिक विचारों (Anchoring ideas) से सुसंगत रूप से जुड़ता है। इस जुड़ाव को सुविधाजनक बनाने के लिए आसुबेल ने 'अग्रिम आयोजक' (Advance Organizers) की संकल्पना दी, जो पूर्व ज्ञान और नई पाठ्य-सामग्री के बीच एक सेतु का कार्य करते हैं। इसके विपरीत, स्किनर और पावलव ने व्यवहारवादी अनुबंधन दिया, जबकि बांडुरा ने सामाजिक अधिगम सिद्धांत विकसित किया। अतः विकल्प C सही उत्तर है।
key_facts: Printed answer key: (C) David Ausubel

Answer explanation extracted from supplied reference material: David Ausubel formulated the theory of meaningful reception learning, emphasizing that new information is learned effectively when anchored to existing relevant concepts within a learner's cognitive structure. Ausubel introduced advance organizers as instructional bridges connecting familiar prior knowledge with unfamiliar new learning material.
